notes: This source/test traceability contract covers only Umbra's bounded non-regional timestamped Delete Object Instance and timestamped Remove Object Instance path in the non-installable 2025 development profile. It exercises lower-bound validation, pending-delete retraction with object reconstitution, exact-bound callback delivery before Time Advance Grant, official timestamp/order/retraction fields, the supplied tag and producing federate, and sender callback exclusion. A cross-service target-departure regression additionally proves that a time-6 removal commits object departure before a separately queued time-7 directed interaction reaches its callback boundary, where the stale directed payload is suppressed. Focused Connection Lost regressions additionally retain time-5 and time-6 removals accepted from the lost regulator through its configured unconditional-divest cleanup until the surviving constrained federate receives Remove Object Instance before its matching time-6 grant; one counterpart keeps the cutoff marker and object state live for a second survivor that requests time 6 only after the first callback, while the DELETE_OBJECTS companion preserves the same timestamped lifecycle rather than replacing it with automatic receive-order removal. A separate mixed nonconstrained/time-constrained scenario now proves a legal post-delivery Retract: a delivered recipient receives Request Retraction, still-pending fanout is withdrawn, and an execution-owned invocation snapshot restores the object, name, known-instance state, and committed split attribute ownership before that callback is exposed. A second scenario confirms an owner who resigns after delivered removal is not revived or notified, while its former attribute remains unowned. The bounded tombstone lifecycle now retains a lightweight terminal record for MessageCanNoLongerBeRetracted while it releases heavyweight deletion payload/snapshot and the deleted-instance marker only after no still-joined recipient remains pending. A focused no-recipient case proves the name is then available for a fresh named registration. Accepted producer TAR/TARA/NMR/NMRA/FQR requests, immediate actual-lookahead increases, successful Retract, and producer resignation are wired to that lifecycle; Disable Time Regulation is intentionally conservative because a later enable can establish a new retraction boundary. Complete alternate-advance, re-enable, save/restore recovery, active in-flight ownership, other producer/recipient resignation, remote transport, packaging, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice.
